summary: The power-completion and strict zero-avoidance derivations check out: F^(1/r) truncation gives deg(R^r-F)<=(r-1)D-1, and the shifted root R+c raises the degree by at most one. The quadratic-jet character-sum bound also holds. Every live count I checked (344 witnesses, 16 stages, 1934 proposals, 11 moves, 116319 Horner evaluations, and the 108/110, 102->109, 118->124/122 and 29->30 scores) matches the artifact. The tight-degree p5 counterexample holds only for the square coset, which the note does not state; with the nonsquare coset the constant Q=3 is a perfect strict solution at K2. The header's list of open cases leaves out unsolved saved high-rate mixed sources: N31,K16 seed71 (30/31) and the r=3/r=4 mixed controls.

claims.quote: Thus ALL common-coset inputs are solved perfectly
claims.finding: Verified: F=lambda^r X^D(...) so F^(1/r)=R+O(1/X), giving deg(F-R^r)<=(r-1)D-1; Q(a_i)-t_i=beta*R(a_i)^r since W vanishes on selected points. Saved global thresholds hold (N16K8: 8<=8; N31K16: 16<=16; N127K77: 64<=77; r3 N63K46: 42<=46; r4 N32K24: 24<=24) and the artifact reports all of these global sources perfect. Holds in the zero-including mode, which is the section's scope.

claims.quote: Hence K>=b+1 is a uniform sufficient condition for perfect STRICT common-coset completion
claims.step: Strict Nonzero Powers: Constructive Zero Avoidance
claims.finding: c in {0..M} avoids at most M forbidden values -R(a_i) since M<p; (R+c)^r-R^r has degree <=(r-1)D=b. Artifact: all ten strict controls report NATIVE_COMPLETION_WITNESS with full score (the r=4 strict sibling uses K25=b+1).

claims.quote: all25 native polynomials fail perfect strict satisfaction
claims.finding: The coset orientation is not stated, and the claim depends on it. Exhaustive check: with the common square coset (orientation 0, the one tests/test_prime_character_opi.py uses), 0/25 polynomials are perfect. With the common nonsquare coset beta=2, the constant Q=3 gives residuals (3,3,3,2), all nonzero nonsquares, so 1/25 is perfect at K2. The counterexample needs 'square coset' added.

claims.quote: Uniform proposals therefore succeed with probability>=1/3
claims.finding: sum_z chi(z^2+a/beta)=-1 for a!=0 gives an accepted count of (p-chi(beta/beta_i)+Z)/2>=(p-1)/2, and (p-1)/(2p)>=1/3 for every odd p>=3. The degree bookkeeping (h=max(0,2D-K+1), deg(2R0L+L^2)<K) also checks out.

claims.quote: For N127,K77,118/118 improves to124/122
claims.step: Adaptive Root-Value Exchange Is Now Executed
claims.finding: Matches the artifact: K77 mixed 118->124 (seed29) and 118->122 (seed71); K39 102->109 for both seeds; 16 repair stages, 1934 proposals, 11 accepted moves and 116319 Horner evaluations; 344 retained witnesses (=4 r2 configs x4 sources x17 + 2 higher-r configs x4 x9). The pass bound N-initial_score+1 follows from strict improvements.

claims.quote: K39 and general fixed-input/asymptotic solvability remain open
claims.finding: The open-case list names only K39, but other saved high-rate mixed sources are also not perfect in the artifact. N31,K16 mixed seed71 is best 30/31 (r=2, R+rho=16/31+1/2>1, so in the published perfect-search regime). The r=3 N63,K46 mixed sources are 55/63 and 56/63 (R+rho~1.06>1), and the r=4 N32,K24 mixed sources are 28/32 and 27/32. The superseding norm attack covers only N127,K77. The Live Controls paragraph also reports only the r=3/r=4 global controls ('also perfect') and omits these mixed scores.

summary: The norm criterion, the K>max(|A|,D) budget, the Cayley strict-root rotation, the rho=1 all-parameter counterexample and the IID-shift first-trial bound all check out. I recomputed D0=(0,4,14,16) with roots 0,9,16, and confirmed that Q=13 is strict-perfect with nu=5 a nonsquare. The artifact matches the executed claims: perfect 127/127 in 1 and 15 trials, degrees 69 and 64, sufficient dimensions 70 and 65, and K39 not applicable. The research-decision summary of what the previous experiment left open omits the N31,K16 mixed seed71 source (30/31) and the r=3/r=4 mixed controls. The norm budget can never hold at N31,K16, so 'does not apply to the saved K39 inputs' is not the full list of inapplicable saved inputs.

claims.quote: a monic polynomial is a norm exactly when every odd-degree irreducible has even multiplicity
claims.finding: Correct: an even-degree irreducible splits into conjugates over F_(p^2); an odd-degree one stays irreducible and has norm f^2. Leading constants are norms because N(c)=c^(p+1) is onto Fp^*.

claims.quote: The exact sufficient degree condition is
claims.finding: With Q=Q0+R^2, deg Q0=|A| (lambda V_A term) and deg R^2=D (F=rho^2*monic of degree D, so H has degree D/2), the condition is K>max(|A|,D). On B, Q-t_i=R^2-F(a_i)=nu Z^2. Artifact: sufficient_RS_dimension 70 and 65; witness degrees 69 and 64.

claims.quote: has a NONZERO quadratic numerator in s, since the original pair is nonzero
claims.step: Strict Roots Without A Field-Size Search
claims.finding: alpha_s has norm (1-nu s^2)/(1-nu s^2)=1. R'=0 gives nu R s^2+2nu Z s+R and Z'=0 gives nu Z s^2+2R s+Z, each nonzero when (R,Z)!=(0,0) and p is odd. That gives <=2N bad s, so 2N+1 distinct candidates suffice when p>2N.

claims.quote: NONE of the23 parameters is a norm, although OPI itself is easy
claims.step: Try To Disprove The Pencil, Then Repair It
claims.finding: Recomputed V_A-V_B over F23: coefficients (0,4,14,16), roots {0,9,16}. Q=13 gives residual 13 (square) on A and 17,14,5,7 (all nonsquares) on B. The moving linear factor can fix at most one odd linear multiplicity. The artifact's expanded repair reaches 8/8 in 5 base factorizations.

claims.quote: so F/rho^2 is a uniform monic degree-D polynomial
claims.finding: Conditioned on the A shifts and lambda, rho, the B residuals (plus the auxiliary value) are uniform, and interpolation is a bijection. Irreducibles of even degree are norms with no roots, so success is >=I_p(D)/p^D, about 1/D (D=58 and 64 for the saved patterns, matching norm_target_degree in the artifact). The 1/(2N) claim follows since the budget forces D<K<=N.

claims.quote: but left mixed high-rate controls at124/127 and122/127
claims.finding: The previous experiment's artifact also leaves N31,K16 mixed seed71 at 30/31 (r=2, rate 16/31>1/2) and the r=3/r=4 mixed controls below perfect. The norm attack was not run on N31, and its budget K>max(|A|,D) cannot hold there: |A|+|B|=31 forces max(|A|,D)>=16=K. Neither this summary nor 'It does not apply to the saved K39 inputs' reports that case.

summary: The recursion, the PSC-degradation argument for rounding up overlaps, and the TV=sum_F m_i accounting are consistent. The artifact's TV bounds equal the sums of the retained per-coordinate upper bounds over the smallest-mean sets. The reported numbers match the artifacts: 16/78/361/1614, the 3/8 follow-up at 0.0234306, and N32768 at 0.0102208 with 65534 combinations and 1,008,335,816 visits. The headline and the half-rate sentence present a single certified length (N32768 on one grid) as a family construction. Half-rate fails at every coarse length N<=4096, and the certificate rests on review-pending degradation/hybrid derivations. The outcomes table also drops the N16 row that the artifact reports.

claims.quote: The preceding hybrid argument gives average uniform-sign Gibbs TV at most
claims.finding: Consistent with the hybrid in POLAR_CONDITIONAL_SAMPLER: epsilon_F there is sum|P-1/2|=(1/2)sum m_i, and the average conditional TV is <=2 epsilon_F. Artifact check: uniform_sign_average_Gibbs_TV_upper equals the sum of all_source_mean_absolute_bias_upper over the frozen set (=2x frozen_prefix_bias_sum_upper), e.g. N32768.

claims.quote: Product and averaged channel combinations preserve this order, and root fidelity cannot decrease under degradation
claims.finding: The Gram identity <psi_0(d)|psi_1(d)>*<psi_0(a/d)|psi_1(a/d)>=a gives the isometry. Discarding the environment degrades the channel, and any degrading map on one input system commutes with the BPQM combinations. Fidelity is monotone under CPTP maps, so rounded-up overlaps upper-bound m_i. The derivation is stated as review pending.

claims.quote: Largest set certified at average TV<=0.1
claims.finding: The rows shown match the artifact (16/64, 78/256=0.304688, 361/1024=0.352539, 1614/4096=0.394043, with TV uppers 0.0826, 0.0935, 0.0998, 0.0995). However, the artifact also has an N16 instance (max 2 constraints, rate 1/8, TV upper 0.0599) that the table omits, so the table is not 'all coarse controls'.

claims.quote: This finite result removes the missing public-set construction premise for the stated half-rate family
claims.finding: Only one half-rate length is certified (N32768, G256, r3: 0.0102208<0.010221, matching the artifact). Every coarse half-rate target at N16..4096 is UNKNOWN, and no other length or grid is certified at half rate, so no family over N is constructed. The bound also depends on the review-pending degradation/hybrid derivations. The next sentence concedes that there is no fixed-grid asymptotic theorem.

claims.quote: This pass removes that blocker for concrete non-prefix families
claims.finding: The headline drops conditions stated elsewhere. The guarantee is average over uniform signs only, and the certified instances are finite: rates up to 1614/4096 at TV<=0.1, the post-exploration 3/8 at N4096, and half rate only at N32768. The certificates rest on review-pending degradation/duality derivations. 'Families' is not established by these finite certificates.

claims.quote: rate3/8 follow-up at N4096 has certified average TV<=0.023431
claims.finding: Artifact explicit_three_eighths_rate_followup: 1536 constraints, 2560 spins, TV upper 0.0234306<=0.023431, rate_chosen_after_exploratory_bound_budget flagged. 3/8=0.375>1-c=0.35 as stated. The TV equals the sum of the N4096 per-coordinate upper bounds over the listed frozen set.

summary: The reverse-order hybrid, the triangle inequalities to 2 epsilon_F, prefix exactness and the source/CQ index-reversal identity check out. The calibration table matches the artifact, and I hand-verified the N2 row (0.08/0.72 conditional TVs, epsilon_F=2/5). I also recomputed that {0,1,2,4} are the four smallest exact prefix biases at N8 under the G^T convention. The weak point is the follow-up header. It says the design note 'resolves' this note's public-set premise, but that premise (epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction) is asymptotic, and the design note certifies one half-rate length on review-pending derivations, which the header omits.

claims.quote: Thus TV(P_U,Qjoint)<=epsilon_F
claims.finding: Standard hybrid: replacing each frozen conditional by a fair bit costs E|P(U_i=1|prefix)-1/2| in TV, summed over F. N2 check: epsilon_F=0.82*(1/2-0.01/0.82)+0.18*0=2/5, matching frozen_prefix_bias_sum in the artifact.

claims.quote: is at most that joint discrepancy. Triangle inequalities then give BOTH
claims.finding: sum_s Q(s)TV(Q_s,P_s)<=TV(Qjoint,P)+TV(Q_F,P_F)<=epsilon_F+delta, and the same holds with P(s) weights. Full-rank H_F makes uniform J give uniform s. Artifact N2: uniform average 0.4 and native 0.144 are both <=2 epsilon_F=0.8.

claims.quote: For a contiguous initial frozen prefix, however, the remaining chain is already conditioned on every constraint
claims.finding: Correct, since all constraints precede the sampled coordinates. The artifact rows N4{0,1} and N8{0,1,2} have zero TV for all syndromes.

claims.quote: The last set selects the four smallest EXACT source prefix biases
claims.finding: Recomputed exact prefix biases at N8, p=7/40 with U=G^T E: m=(0.0319,0.1785,0.1785,0.596,0.1785,0.6313,0.7017,0.9581), so {0,1,2,4} is the smallest-4 set. Its half-sum 0.28369 matches 14525010721/51200000000. The table values 0.00416611/0.05596208 match the artifact.

claims.quote: Hence the CQ information at i equals the source conditional entropy at N-1-i
claims.step: Why This Is Relevant To The Quantum Proposal
claims.finding: For F=[[1,0],[1,1]], F^T=RFR, which extends to tensor powers. The artifact N2/N4 lists are exact reversals (e.g. N4 Holevo [0.2400,0.7018,0.7573,0.9769] vs entropies [0.9769,0.7573,0.7018,0.2400]), with errors ~1e-16. Numerics, as conceded.

claims.quote: It resolves the missing public-set premise below for that finite family
claims.finding: This note's premise is 'epsilon_F->0 with a polynomial construction' for a code family. The follow-up certifies a single half-rate length (N32768) at fixed TV 0.0102; half-rate is UNKNOWN at every coarse N<=4096, so no epsilon_F->0 sequence is given. The header also drops that the certificate rests on POLAR_SOURCE_DESIGN's review-pending degradation/duality derivations.
